title: Multimodal analysis of the interactions between hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), HCC treatment, muscle status, and nutritional status, as well as their relationship to quality of life
summary: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a form of liver cancer that often develops in patients with cirrhosis of the liver. The disease is frequently severe and is associated with problems such as weight loss, muscle wasting, weakness, and psychological distress. These factors impair quality of life and can influence how well treatments work. The “MyoLife-HCC” study therefore investigates how nutrition, muscle condition, physical activity, and mental health are interrelated and how they change over the course of treatment. To this end, the study includes physical tests, questionnaires, activity measurements, and blood analyses. The goal is to identify specific biological markers in the blood that indicate how the body and muscles change as the disease progresses. In the long term, these findings should help tailor treatments better to individual patients and improve their quality of life.
conditions: Other and unspecified cirrhosis of liver

interventions.name: Arm 1: Patients with hepatocellular carcinoma will undergo comprehensive assessments every 3 months over a 1-year period regarding their nutritional and muscle status, physical activity, psychological stress, and quality of life (QoL). In addition, their plasma proteome will be analyzed.

Arm 2: Control group – Patients with liver cirrhosis without malignancy will undergo comprehensive assessments every 6 months over a 1-year period regarding nutritional and muscle status, physical activity, psychological stress, and QoL. In addition, the plasma proteome will be analyzed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Arm 1 - HCC: New diagnosis or strong suspicion based on clinical and imaging findings (ultrasound, MRI, CT)
- Arm 2 - Liver cirrhosis: Confirmed diagnosis based on a biopsy or the typical combination of clinical, laboratory, and imaging findings; if necessary, also based on shear-wave elastography with no evidence of malignancy
Exclusion criteria:
- Pregnancy or breastfeeding
- Pacemaker or implanted defibrillator
- Inability to complete questionnaires
- Known severe comorbidities that represent a competing cause of malnutrition, sarcopenia, or death: COPD GOLD 3 or 4, heart failure NYHA 3 or 4
 Pre-existing malignant tumors in addition to HCC or a well-founded suspicion thereof within the last 3 years
- Conditions affecting muscle or joint function, as well as major amputations that lead to muscle atrophy or render muscle function tests unfeasible
